A year on I think a 3060ti is a pretty decent card for a lot of people.  Availability is still constrained and prices are still 100% more than MSRP (or more) - when people have a chance to pick up a 3060ti I don't think they will be disappointed.  In my mind it gets you into a couple of important technologies: DisplayPort 1.4, HDMI 2.1, GDDR6, and a 256bit memory interface (which from a performance standpoint you really don't want to go below...the 1080ti has a 256bit interface...anything less is a step back to 2011 technology).  

For reference everything that is being currently manufactured 'south' of the 3060ti in terms of price/ performance has either a 192bit memory interface, or worse yet a 128bit memory interface.  As long as you are comfortable with 1440p/ 1080p as your sandbox you'll be able to run AAA titles well and have driver support for a good long while AND take advantage of the newest generation monitor/ display speeds (just don't skimp on your cables).
